purpose: Continue the Atlas after the original P00–P17 implementation roadmap with a governed programme to resolve every public data slot without inventing values or weakening source standards.
relationship_to_v1_release: This roadmap is intentionally separate from data/project-roadmap.json. P00–P17 remain the v1.0 implementation/release ledger; P18–P26 govern the subsequent data-completion programme and must not alter P17 release-count semantics.
completion_definition: Every one of the 20,115 governed public slot instances is resolved by a published/direct observation, a transparently derived/modelled value permitted by policy, a verified external observation, or an explicit governed closure state such as not applicable, source not published, boundary unresolved, or retired/replaced. Unknown blanks must equal zero.
rules: Do not manufacture a value merely to raise completion.
Do not inherit a parent-geography value into a child geography unless the indicator policy explicitly permits a derived cross-level measure.
Promote existing canonical observations before acquiring new data.
Use primary official sources where practical and retain source, period, unit, denominator and uncertainty metadata.
Survey estimates must retain required uncertainty or sample metadata before activation.
When a proposed slot has no defensible comparable source, replace, retire or explicitly close it rather than scrape weak substitutes.
Generated registries and completeness outputs must be reproducible from source snapshots and build scripts.
A phase is complete only when its governed queue is zero or every remaining row has an explicit approved closure state, and the full Atlas validation/P16 gates remain green where the website changes.

Every acceptance item is satisfied and independently re-verified by npm run p23:validate on the exact closing commit: all 290 constituencies reconcile to the canonical geography registry (validate-constituency-voter-readiness.mjs, validate-constituency-mps.mjs); election periods and boundary vintages are explicit throughout the Form 34B evidence corpus (251 evidence files, all pass validate-form34b-source-verifications.mjs); NG-CDF observations retain source fiscal period and implementation status (validate-ngcdf-allocation.mjs); no county value is inherited as a constituency observation (LOCAL_INDICATOR_CASCADE_VALIDATE_OK inherited=0); and the constituency build is deterministic (npm run build:data is byte-identical across repeated runs). The 290/290 constituency IND-TURNOUT-HISTORY rows are fully resolved: 186 source-verified and promoted, 104 governed official_unavailable closures with documented, non-fabrication reasons (denominator conflicts, arithmetic mismatches, structural scan defects, portal access problems, and one source-image illegibility case -- Kisauni, the last to close). completion_phase='P23' no longer appears anywhere in the live ledger.

progress.note: Research confirmed Kenya has no uniform official national ward-level development-fund programme comparable to NG-CDF: the National Government Constituencies Development Fund Act, 2015 (as amended) allocates and administers the Fund per constituency, not per ward; county-run 'Ward Development Fund' programmes (e.g. Nairobi City County, Kiambu County, Kakamega County) exist under separate County Assembly Acts with different amounts and rules and are not present in all 47 counties; and the County Wards (Equitable Development) Bill that would create one national ward fund remains unenacted. All 1,450 IND-WARD-FUND-ALLOCATION ward slots are therefore closed not_applicable under data/p24/ward-fund-allocation-closure-contract.json rather than divided from a parent total. Separately, the ten already-documented Mandera East/Lafey ward-voter slots (30 rendered rows across the overview/people/representation tabs) are formally closed boundary_unresolved under data/p24/ward-voters-boundary-hold-contract.json, citing the same spatial hold preserved since P23A/P23X. Combined with the separately merged ward-census publication-gap closure (data/p24/ward-census-closure-contract.json, 1,450 slots), the ward health-facility-density closure (data/p24/ward-health-facility-density-closure-contract.json, 1,450 slots) and the ward turnout-history closure below (1,450 slots), only one still-unresolved 1,450-ward family remains: IND-MCA-IDENTITY.

ward_turnout_history_closure.completion_note: All 1,450 ward IND-TURNOUT-HISTORY slots are closed as governed official_unavailable. No ready-made official ward-level turnout aggregate exists; producing real values would require a dedicated Form 34A (re-summed to ward) or Form 36B ward-tally source-verification pipeline of the same class as the P23 Form34B effort, at up to five times the geographic unit count. No constituency value is copied down and no proxy/estimate is used. Each closure carries a refresh trigger for later official supersession.

progress.next_family: Remaining P24 ward families (MCA identity, service/facility aggregation, land-area derivation, ward-fund treatment) are unresolved by this closure and require separate, dedicated tranches.
progress.closure_note: Closed 2026-09-16, immediately after P23 (its declared dependency). Every acceptance item is satisfied and independently re-verified by npm run p24:validate on the exact closing commit: all 1,450 statistical wards remain represented in the completion ledger; boundary-vintage mismatches (the Mandera East/Lafey spatial hold, 30 rows) remain explicit rather than silently assigned; ward-fund slots are marked not_applicable (1,450 rows) since no uniform national ward-level development-fund programme exists; no constituency/county value is inherited downward (LOCAL_INDICATOR_CASCADE_VALIDATE_OK inherited=0); and the Mandera East/Lafey geometry constraint remains transparently unresolved rather than force-matched. completion_phase='P24' no longer appears anywhere in the live ledger.

progress.closure_note: Closed 2026-09-16. All seven acceptance criteria are met and machine-verified by scripts/p26/validate-permanent-completion-gate.mjs, now wired permanently into `npm test` (so it runs on every future push, not just this one): (1) resolved slot count (20,115) equals total governed slot count (20,115) -- zero unresolved; (2) unknown_missing = 0; (3) hidden active canonical observations = 0 (no governed-closure slot has a real, current observation available that it is instead hiding behind a closure status); (4) prohibited parent-to-child inherited observations = 0, with constituency and ward disposition coverage of the 54 active county indicators both at 100%; (5) numeric/categorical evidence coverage is reported separately from governed closure coverage (10,774 numeric-evidence slots, 53.56%; 9,341 governed-closure slots, 46.44% -- both fully accounted for, summing to the total); (6) every non-numeric closure state carries reason/period_label/source/source_url, structurally enforced by scripts/completeness/validate-slot-ledger.mjs and re-asserted here. Item 7 (full rebuild, validation, P16 audit and Pages deployment on the exact completion SHA) is verified operationally: npm run build:data, npm test (which now includes p26:validate itself) and npm run p16:static all pass on this exact commit before it is pushed, and the existing 'Validate Atlas data' and 'P23 Form 34B source verification' GitHub Actions workflows run the same checks again on push to main. This is the first commit in the project's history where every governed slot is simultaneously resolved with zero unresolved, zero unknown, and zero hidden active observations -- a real, machine-verified 100%, not an estimate.
